approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from the current session's accepted scored molecules. It retains the best 64 molecules, draws breeding parents across score quantiles, and builds a surplus pool with connected-fragment crossover and successive local atom, bond and ring mutations. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities, duplicate rejection and a sulfur rule based on the actual scored generating parents govern admission. A Gaussian process fits all accepted observations using integer Morgan environment counts and generalized Tanimoto similarity. Its predictive mean plus correlated residual draws select distinct molecules from each fresh pool, and their real feedback updates the archive and breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove repeated-environment information only from the predictive mean used to choose molecules. Compute a second Gaussian process from presence indicators of the same cached Morgan rows, and use its mean with the exact original count-model residual. The earlier full-binary removal changed both mean and covariance; this probe holds the residual consumer fixed to answer the narrower location question. The other count probe changes covariance instead, and the feature and mutation siblings change different interfaces. None of their changes enter this Child. The earlier removal losses and better count predictions motivate a predicted loss here, while the experiment can also return a gain or no material effect.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behaviour is low productive yield from the evaluated offspring, whose ranking depends on a count-informed predictive location of unresolved consumer-specific value. Reading all fifteen n-1744a1494180 optimizer logs gives 648 strict best-generating-parent beats among 4350 accepted offspring and 255 sequential incumbent improvements; all remaining observations still remain in learning and the score comparison. The complete Parent mean is 0.59645311428869 with population SD 0.03397032998399878, and its sulfur-gate addition gained only 0.0007834645552323346 against its own Parent, below the frozen +0.002 performance goal. The complete current all-output binary removal n-b9f2c3328d4c loses 0.038794771343121, with seed deltas -0.08614960727939203/+0.005329208758406034/-0.03556391550837701 and all five task means lower. Its recorded passive count model predicts its real accepted labels better (chronological MSE about 0.01065 versus binary 0.01807, mean within-batch rank correlation about 0.614 versus 0.389), but mean and covariance changed jointly. The earlier ungated n-e00db808bbb4 removal also lost 0.051295849138213355 under a different Parent. Neither answer isolates active location under the current sulfur gate. The exact-environment n-fe734eb5c1df location control establishes an auditable mean-versus-residual boundary, rather than evidence for binary location: it targets a different frozen external recipe, uses a different code Parent/lock, and all fifteen of its trajectories repeat the original GP realizations. This probe answers only the new current-Parent location criterion.

literature_review.conclusion: I read the recorded current full-binary review in n-b9f2c3328d4c and the exact-environment location-control review/source in n-fe734eb5c1df, then ran the actual queries above and reopened the primary Tanimoto paper, GPML conditional equations, official pinned RDKit release tests and API. The representation algebra and release interface from the count review remain applicable; its whole-binary endpoint answer is preserved but cannot answer a mean-only consumer test. The external control's boundary technique applies without importing its model, recipe or lock, and its efficacy does not transfer. Adopt exact support thresholding for a second complete GP and replace only the active mean, retaining the complete original Count residual and all numerical receipts. Direct current and ungated full-removal losses and better Count predictions motivate the decrease hypothesis as an inference; the new natural-history matched experiment decides the conditional location contribution. Reject external models, kernel/normalization/noise changes and random-feature approximations for this isolating control. Literature and passive arithmetic do not identify mediation, universal benefit or the separate performance goal.

finding_summary.headline: Removing count information from predictive location lowers the matched mean by 0.088227
finding_summary.insights:
Count information has positive conditional contribution at predictive location in this sulfur-gated search while the original Count residual remains active. That answers the narrower consumer question left open by the earlier removal of both location and covariance. It does not identify which predictive or descendant behavior mediates the endpoint loss, separate a mean/covariance interaction, or make the shared-control probes independent or additive. The selected-stream predictor comparison leaves every unselected alternative without a score or continued history.

The result is heterogeneous but not confined to one exceptional cell. The seed 1 docking endpoint falls from 0.999999 to 0.268144 and contributes 0.048790 of the 0.088227 mean loss. The Parent's late seed 0 deco_hop breakthrough also remains in the primary comparison; removing either cell descriptively still leaves a material loss. Productive first typed cores increased from 262 to 271, and generic cores from 163 to 207, yet their summed best-parent gains and descendant progress weakened. More productive-core arrivals and reuse are therefore insufficient substitutes for the magnitude of accepted progress. Molecular evidence associates some weak streams with oversized connected ring assemblies rather than the compact complete aryl/amine or carbonyl arrangements seen at stronger labels. Useful compact leaders remain possible, while reactive attachments, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist in both nodes. Those chemistry associations explain the limits of the generated output without assigning a component-specific chemical cause or certifying synthesis, stability or pharmacology. Broader composition attribution, transfer and historical catalog rechecks remain open; this fixed consumer probe has its complete exposed answer.
finding_summary.results:
Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.596453 to 0.508226, a loss of 0.088227 against the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. All three seed means and all five task means declined; 12 of 15 endpoints fell and three improved. Seed dispersion rose from 0.033970 to 0.067672. The change reached real search in every session: all 435 fresh-pool selected sets differed from the same-input Count reference, with 2,524 strict masked-winner changes and 2,116 accepted identities absent from its passive selected sets. 2,043 of those entered later fits, 915 were later drawn as scored parents and 483 generated accepted descendants. The original Count residual and normal arrays were retained exactly, with no numerical fallback.

On the same 4,350 real selected labels, Binary mean squared error was worse in all 15 sessions: 0.012991 versus 0.007384 for the passive Count mean. Mean accepted offspring score was 0.284658 versus the Parent's 0.372050; summed positive best-parent gains were 11.038651 versus 17.251535, and cumulative incumbent gains were 4.496007 versus 5.819415. These pooled directions coexist with explicitly retained task/seed counterexamples and final-batch censorship.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides and aryl amines coexist with oversized ring assemblies, reactive attachments and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-161b32768a03 produces azaaryl amides, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl heterocycles, phenolic diaryl amines, aryl-linked bridged dicarbonyl rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl systems. Recognizable medicinal frameworks coexist with heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide linkages, reactive acyl/sulfonyl halides and difficult connected-ring geometry. There is ample ring chemistry: digest ring-closure incidence is 0.9552-0.9816 and aromatic-string incidence is 0.9379-0.9724. These are molecule-level SMILES-text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Leading series vary within seeds, and distinct seeds reach different frameworks; structural diversity is moderate, not globally collapsed. All 15 Child and all 15 published code-Parent n-1744a1494180 trajectories were read completely, covering issued Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 and all five independent sessions at 300 accepted observations each. Every task has 900 records per node, including 870 optimizer observations. There are no missing paths, omitted tasks, parse failures or absent paired cells. context.comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with no profile-mismatched seeds. No complete Child session is identical to its paired Parent session. Published Parent trajectories, including the late seed-0 carbonyl/thione breakthrough at evaluation 281, remain the comparison authority. These are complete paired descriptions, not independent historical replications. A read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 graph audit shows pooled optimizer median heavy-atom counts of 25, 54, 47, 32 and 27 in the fixed task order, versus Parent 24, 31, 29, 31 and 27. Thus some streams preserve compact compounds while others elaborate very large aromatic assemblies. All digest charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0, although free aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic centres are present. Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 2139 of 4350 Child optimizer observations versus 2455 Parent observations. The lack of charge markers is not a lack of basic nitrogen. The graph audit and all source-path hashes are in .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r32-slot2-molecular/trajectory_chemistry_receipt.json; descriptor and motif counts are readings of the recorded SMILES with the denominators defined there. Graph validity and recorded labels do not establish stability, synthesis, conformational access or pharmacology. Only accepted trajectory chemistry is covered, not unselected pools or rejected alternatives. The recurring gaps were originally recorded in indexed n-c55c3d520a2c, reproduced in n-62daf219c70a, and carried by current Parent n-1744a1494180. Their current recurrence is an output association under this exact Child/Parent profile and Search panel; it does not attribute a liability, score change or chemical capability to the location consumer, sulfur admission rule or another component.

per_task.generated_character: All three seed leaders have 25 heavy atoms. Seed 0 has a partially unsaturated benzene-connected nitrogen ring joined through an amide to a fluoropyridyl group, with methoxy, methyl and chloromethyl substitution. Seed 1 retains an indole-like aromatic amide/pyridyl system with N-fluoromethyl or N-bromomethyl substitution and additional halomethyl groups. Seed 2 reaches a benzene-connected unsaturated medium-ring closure bearing direct N-Cl and an N-methyl pyridyl amide; other high labels occur on densely fused relatives. Pooled median size is Child 25 versus Parent 24 heavy atoms, with substantial aromatic and carbonyl organization. Seeds 0 and 1 show relatively familiar local bonds, although halomethyl groups remain; seed 2 introduces more difficult topology and N-halogen chemistry. RDKit ring counts in bridged systems depend on the perceived cycle basis and do not certify their geometry.
liabilities: Direct N-Cl in the strongest seed-2 series, benzylic halomethyl groups and some N-halomethyl substitution require environment-specific reactivity assessment; ordinary carbon-bound aryl halogens are a different case.

Unsaturated medium-ring or fused closures are not backed by conformational evidence. Cyclic cumulene proposals also occur, including the cited seven-membered cyclic cumulated system at seed 1 evaluation 100, score 0.2400130776664593.
Pooled accepted output includes 239 of 870 molecules with direct N-halogen bonds and 327 with perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres, despite zero explicit stereocentre-string incidence.
missing_features: Conventional substitution and resolved stereochemical identity are not consistently retained around the best-scoring aromatic/amide arrangement: the highest record has direct N-Cl and an unassigned saturated centre, whereas other successful seeds supply counterexamples without that bond.

The record does not establish an exact missing target pharmacophore. Independent plausible realizations of the favorable compact arrangement remain less evident than close amide, halomethyl and ring-closure variants; rings, heteroaryl nitrogen and amides themselves are already present.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145; a seed-1 methyl-for-methoxy relative at evaluation 15 scores 0.36371550417720466. Seed endpoints are 0.4145039882261785, 0.436818201428663 and 0.47189631731668286, versus published Parent 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598. Removing the amide/second aryl region gives the 16-heavy-atom fluorinated indole at seed 2 evaluation 50 only 0.00034958375642754933; the 47-heavy-atom doubled aromatic amide at seed 1 evaluation 300 scores 7.588461626494105e-24, and NF scores 0.0. The visible association is a compact complete aromatic/amide arrangement, not fluorination, aromatic mass or nitrogen count alone. The high seed-2 N-Cl label does not establish that N-Cl is required: the other seed leaders lack direct N/O-halogen bonds.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 favors a linked azaaromatic and fused nitrogen-rich dione system with fluorinated alkyl groups and a brominated side chain; its best molecule has 34 heavy atoms and mixed aromatic/saturated ring content. Seed 1 develops linked azaaryl/pyrrolic regions with multiple carbamate/urea-like carbonyls, vinyl esters and O-F; its tied leaders have 39 and 40 heavy atoms, while its optimizer median is 61. Seed 2 reaches a 68-heavy-atom, ring-rich assembly of imino/dione, coumarin-like and pyridyl regions with polyenyl substituents and a peroxide linkage; its median is 72. The pooled Child median is 54 heavy atoms versus Parent 31, and accepted Child size extends to 120. Carbon-thione bonds are still generated in 188 of 870 optimizer observations, although the seed leaders are sulfur-free. The compact seed-0 heterocyclic core is recognizable, but the other streams often have extensive elaboration and questionable peripheral chemistry.
liabilities: O-F occurs in 197 of 870 accepted optimizer molecules, and O-O bonds in 112. The seed-2 final series also includes longer O-O-O chains; these are not conventional ether substitutions.
Very large assemblies combine many aromatic regions, polyenes and carbonyl groups. Valence-valid linkage and high ring counts do not demonstrate an accessible synthesis or useful physical properties.
The seed-0 leader has three unassigned tetrahedral centres; the carbonyl/thione Parent breakthrough itself also has chemical liabilities and is not a plausibility certificate.
missing_features: The compact complete carbonyl/thione and azaaryl organization associated with the Parent late breakthrough is not recovered at a comparable label. This is not an inability to make thiones: many accepted Child molecules contain carbon-sulfur double bonds.

Stable peripheral alternatives preserving the successful linked heterocyclic arrangement are not consistently established among leaders. No exact missing target motif or general requirement for a peroxide, O-F group or unusually large scaffold follows from these observations.

Defined stereochemical and conformational identity is missing where the substituted fused seed-0 system creates stereogenic centres; seed-1 and seed-2 leaders need different whole-molecule feasibility assessments.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.548381482770623. Tiny ethane scores 0.5 and the seed-0 16-heavy-atom quinolyl peroxide at evaluation 15 scores 0.5100965759438103. The Child seed endpoints are 0.6223765888264854, 0.5964970257766028 and 0.602179067404313. The 98-heavy-atom seed-2 concatenation at evaluation 200 scores 0.5961911626101901, so enormous aromatic size does not exceed the compact seed-0 leader. Within the large seed-2 series, however, elaboration still carries labels above its initial observations; a universal size penalty cannot be inferred. Published Parent seed 0 reaches 0.8561477222467935 at evaluation 281 with a compact linked azaaryl carbonyl/thione family, retaining O-F and halomethyl chemistry; its seeds 1 and 2 reach 0.6204376881838878 and 0.6442339647723496. The Child does not recover that late high-scoring complete organization. Neither sulfur absence nor extra rings identifies the reason.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 26-heavy-atom leader combines two phenolic aryl regions, a primary aliphatic amine and a saturated azetidine, with aryl chlorine and a chloromethyl group. Nearby high-labelled molecules include additional aminal-like nitrogen environments or aryl hydroperoxide substitution. Seed 1 instead retains a much larger substituted aryl/azaaryl system with a bridged diaza ring, ketone/enol functionality and a carbon-bound sulfonyl chloride; its leader has 44 heavy atoms and five unassigned tetrahedral centres. Seed 2 reaches a 27-heavy-atom cross-connected chlorinated aromatic system bearing an aniline and a side-chain N-methylpyrrolidine. The seed-0, seed-1 and seed-2 optimizer medians are 21, 56 and 52 heavy atoms; pooled median is Child 47 versus Parent 29. Thus the highest-scoring compact amine stream is not representative of the entire output. Free basic amines are plainly available despite neutral SMILES.
liabilities: The best seed-0 compound contains a benzylic chloride and an unassigned centre; a nearby near-ceiling label contains an aryl hydroperoxide. Saturated azetidine itself is recognizable chemistry and should not be treated as an impossible ring.
Sulfonyl chloride, O-F and N-F occur in the larger aryl/bridged-nitrogen series; the seed-1 leader has multiple unresolved stereocentres and synthetic complexity.

Dense aromatic cross-connections in seed 2 require geometric assessment. Large concatenations reach 119 heavy atoms across the task and do not consistently reproduce the high labels of compact amines.
missing_features: Consistent access to the compact available-amine/aromatic arrangement is missing in the larger streams; the molecules already contain basic centres, so a shortage of ring amines is not supported.

Defined stereochemical identity and demonstrated conformations of the successful substituted cyclic amines are absent. No exact additional receptor pharmacophore can be inferred from the supplied molecules and labels.

Conventional peripheral chemistry is not consistently retained: a successful primary-amine/azetidine example avoids direct heteroatom-halogen bonds, but nearby high labels carry peroxide, and the weaker seed-1 leader retains sulfonyl chloride.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An early N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine with N-chloro amide scores 0.00016650955053713697; its N-sulfonyl ketone counterpart scores 0.00021169315013374197. The seed-0 evaluation-11 free methylamine/acid/biaryl molecule scores 0.026070456802821305, so an amine alone is insufficient. Compact phenolic diaryl/azetidine and primary-amine organization reaches 0.9960479658720314 at seed 0 evaluation 281. A nearby molecule with an aryl O-O group scores 0.9958063651120048, showing that a favorable label can retain a liability. The seed-1 100-heavy-atom sulfonyl/aryl concatenation at evaluation 100 scores 0.028858376914683126; its eventual 44-heavy-atom leader reaches only 0.2681439276319477. Seed 2 reaches 0.9333974293649306 with a smaller aryl/cyclic-amine arrangement. Published Parent endpoints are 0.9912539132815379, 0.9999994532254913 and 0.9817975835038065; its strongest seed-1 molecule is a much smaller diaryl diaza-ring thioether. The observed association concerns available amine placement and complete aryl context, not nitrogen, sulfur or ring counts in isolation. The labels are not experimental affinity or selectivity measurements.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2 develops a propyl/ethoxy-substituted aryl amino ring linked through a partially unsaturated bicyclic dicarbonyl system to a chlorophenyl group; its leader has 33 heavy atoms. Seed 0 has a 34-heavy-atom azaaryl/phenyl, ether-containing bridged nitrogen/dicarbonyl framework. Seed 1 has 33-heavy-atom leaders combining an ethoxybenzyl amino region, an indole-like region, a small bridged lactam and a nitrogen-oxygen ring segment. Aromatic regions, carbonyls, ethers and ring nitrogens are abundant. Pooled median size is Child 32 versus Parent 31 heavy atoms. These are distinct seed families with repeated local variants, not a ring-deficient or globally collapsed output. Some local functional groups are familiar, but complex bridge connectivity, N-O environments and unspecified stereochemistry keep whole-molecule synthesis questionable.
liabilities: Dense bridged and partly unsaturated nitrogen rings require whole-molecule geometric assessment; the leading examples have unassigned tetrahedral centres.

Nitrogen-oxygen ring environments and late peroxide links require their own local stability assessment. Eight accepted optimizer observations have a perceived cyclic cumulated carbon centre, including the cited six-membered example; ordinary carbonyl groups are chemically different.
Pooled output contains 573 of 870 molecules with unassigned tetrahedral centres and 38 with O-O bonds. Near-identical functional counts do not establish plausible independent scaffold coverage.
missing_features: Simple, geometrically credible independent realizations of the successful aryl/amine/carbonyl organization are not consistently represented among leading molecules. There is no evidence for a lack of aromatic rings, carbonyls or nitrogen centres, and no exact missing target structure can be read from these labels.

The generated saturated and bridged centres lack explicit stereochemical identity. The Parent has different favorable ring organizations, but neither Parent nor Child trajectories validate their accessible conformations or synthesis.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 27-heavy-atom leader is a fused N-methyl imino/carbonyl heterocycle bearing a cyclopentadiene, fluoromethyl/fluoroethyl groups, carbon-bound fluorine and an N-fluoro carbamoyl group. A related high-labelled structure uses a cyclobutene. Seed 1 reaches a 27-heavy-atom bis-imino fused nitrogen system attached to a difluoroaryl region with an acyl fluoride and a fluoromethyl substituent; this leader has no direct N/O-halogen bond. Seed 2 reaches a 26-heavy-atom fused dione with N-F and a fluorinated, methoxy/enol-substituted cyclopentadiene. Median size is 27 heavy atoms in both Child and Parent. liabilities: Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 266 of 870 accepted optimizer observations, versus Parent 425; O-halogen bonds occur in 140 versus Parent 82. These opposing motif changes cannot be summarized as uniformly improved chemistry.
Acyl fluoride in the seed-1 leader, N-F in the seed-0 and seed-2 leaders, and enolic/imino systems need separate functional-group and state assessments.

Unsaturated small-ring relatives and connected-ring alternatives are not conformationally validated. The seed-0 and seed-1 best molecules have no perceived tetrahedral centre, whereas the seed-2 best has an unassigned one; the stereochemical gap is conditional, not universal.
missing_features: Conventional stable substitutions maintaining the favorable compact polar organization are not consistently present at the highest labels. The no-N/O-halogen seed-1 leader is a useful counterexample to a universal N-F requirement, but its acyl fluoride leaves a separate reactivity concern.

Tautomeric and conformational identity of imino/enolic and unsaturated ring systems is not established, and some generated saturated centres remain stereochemically unresolved. The trajectories do not identify an exact missing target pharmacophore or show that adding more heteroatoms would fill it.

Child endpoints are 0.6001834463132963, 0.566413342616881 and 0.48264467070275885, versus published Parent 0.6942804632817005, 0.4999004646832901 and 0.6201223048692813. In the seed-0 leader series, replacing N-F with an additional fluoromethyl substituent gives 0.5182121075714027, still a substantial label; changing the cyclopentadiene into the cited nitrogen-containing ring at evaluation 300 gives only 0.05472557844954751 despite retaining N-F. transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally documented in n-c55c3d520a2c and reproduced in n-62daf219c70a, this gap was carried by n-1744a1494180 and is re-observed in n-161b32768a03 versus that exact Parent on the current profile, Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, and 300 accepted observations per independent session. Of 4350 Child optimizer observations, 546 contain N-halogen, 472 O-halogen, 86 S-halogen and 219 O-O bonds; categories overlap. These are graph observations, not stability measurements. Strong compact amide and amine examples avoid direct N/O-halogen bonds, while other leading families retain N-Cl, N-F, O-F, acyl fluoride, sulfonyl chloride or peroxide chemistry. The Parent sulfur-envelope source condition does not cover every such environment.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments when modifying favorable aromatic and heterocyclic regions.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate conventional local alternatives while preserving supported functional-group relationships and distinguishing carbon-bound halogens from heteroatom-halogen bonds. Assess complete bond environments, including the permitted sulfur classes, without conflating envelope membership with synthesis or stability. Preserve useful amines and ordinary sulfur chemistry where feedback supports them. These associations do not prove that a broader filter improves scores or assign the liability to a particular component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c, recurs through n-62daf219c70a and n-1744a1494180, and persists in current-profile n-161b32768a03 on the complete issued Search panel at 300 accepted observations per session. The Child has an unsaturated medium-ring amide leader, dense cross-connected aromatic and bridged nitrogen frameworks, and 10 accepted optimizer observations with cyclic cumulated carbon centres versus Parent 6. Familiar saturated azetidine and pyrrolidine motifs also occur at favorable labels. Rich rings and fewer small-ring observations therefore do not establish accessible geometry, and small-ring presence is not itself an infeasibility finding.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a representable ring graph from credible unsaturation and connected-ring geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need awareness of ring size, unsaturation geometry and bridge connectivity, with feasible alternative topologies retaining learned chemical relationships. Aromatic notation and graph sanitization do not supply conformational evidence. Keep ordinary small, fused and medium rings distinguishable from unsupported constrained bond arrangements. This is an output-feasibility gap, without a measured component-specific cause or guaranteed score benefit.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
